books.title: Resurrection
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.desc: Serving on a jury, a Russian prince recognises the accused as the young woman he seduced years before, and sets out to undo the wrong he did her.
about: Prince Dmitri Nekhludoff, a wealthy landowner, is called to serve on a jury in Moscow. Among the accused in a poisoning case he recognises Maslova, once known as Katusha, the young girl he seduced and abandoned years earlier at his aunts' estate, and whose fall into poverty and prostitution began with that betrayal. When a careless error by the court sends her to hard labour in Siberia, Nekhludoff resolves to win her release and to atone for what he has done.

Tolstoy's last novel follows its hero through courts, prisons and convict convoys, and is a severe criticism of the justice system, the official Church, private ownership of land and the indifference of the privileged classes. Its theme is moral awakening, the "resurrection" of the title, told in a plain and direct style.

Resurrection was published in serial form in the magazine Niva in 1899 and appeared as a book at the end of that year. Tolstoy gave the proceeds to help the Doukhobors, a persecuted religious community, emigrate to Canada. This English translation is by Louise Maude, who translated many of Tolstoy's works with her husband Aylmer Maude.

books.title: The Cossacks
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.desc: Tired of Moscow society, a young nobleman joins the army in the Caucasus and falls under the spell of a Cossack village and of the beautiful Maryánka.

editions.credit: Traduction : Louise Maude (1855-1939) et Aylmer Maude (1858-1938)

about: Dmitri Olénin, a young Moscow nobleman weary of idle society life, leaves for the Caucasus as a cadet and is quartered in a Cossack village on the Terek River. He is drawn to the free, physical life of the Cossacks, goes hunting with the old hunter Uncle Eróshka, befriends the young warrior Lukáshka and falls in love with Maryánka, the girl Lukáshka hopes to marry.

The short novel contrasts the artificial life of the city with the natural world of the mountains and the Cossack community, and explores a young man's search for happiness and self-sacrifice. Tolstoy drew on his own years in the Caucasus in the early 1850s.
The Cossacks was published in 1863 in the journal The Russian Messenger. This English translation is by Louise and Aylmer Maude.

books.title: Poor Folk
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.desc: In letters exchanged across a St Petersburg courtyard, a poor ageing copying clerk and a young orphan share their hardships and their affection.
about: Makar Alexievitch Dievushkin, a middle-aged copying clerk in a St Petersburg government office, lives in a corner of a crowded lodging house. Across the courtyard lives Barbara (Varvara) Alexievna, a young woman who has lost her family and her home. The two write to each other almost every day, describing their poverty, their memories and their small joys, while Makar spends what little he has on gifts for her.

Dostoevsky's first novel is told entirely in letters. It shows the humiliation and dignity of the "little man" of the city, the power of money over human relations, and the tenderness that survives in hard conditions.

Poor Folk was published in January 1846 in the St Petersburg Collection, an almanac, and was praised by the critic Vissarion Belinsky, which launched Dostoevsky's literary career. This English translation is by C. J. Hogarth.

books.title: Mother
books.author: Maxim Gorky
books.desc: In a Russian factory town, a timid worker's widow comes to share the revolutionary ideas of her son and his comrades.
about: Pelagueya Nilovna Vlasova, widow of a brutal and drunken factory worker, lives in a workers' settlement with her son Pavel. When Pavel gives up drink, starts reading forbidden books and gathers young workers and intellectuals in their home, she is at first afraid for him. Little by little she grows close to his comrades, learns to understand their ideas and begins to take part in their secret work.

Gorky's novel describes the hard life of factory workers and the growth of the socialist movement in Russia, and centres on a simple, religious woman's awakening to political consciousness. It is often regarded as a forerunner of Soviet socialist realism.

Gorky wrote Mother in 1906 while in the United States. It first appeared in English in Appleton's Magazine in 1906, before its Russian publication in 1907. The novel drew on real events, the workers' May Day demonstration of 1902 in Sormovo, near Nizhny Novgorod. This edition reproduces an anonymous English translation.
books.author_short: Russian writer (1868–1936), author of The Lower Depths, Mother and an autobiographical trilogy that begins with My Childhood.
author_long: Alexei Maximovich Peshkov was born on 28 March 1868 in Nizhny Novgorod. His father died when he was a small child, and he was brought up by his grandparents; he left school young to work and later wandered through Russia. He wrote under the pen name Maxim Gorky, "gorky" meaning "bitter" in Russian. He died on 18 June 1936.

His play The Lower Depths (1902) portrays the outcasts of Russian society. His novels include Mother (1906), and his autobiographical trilogy comprises My Childhood (1913–14), In the World (1915–16) and My Universities (1923).

books.title: The Lady with the Dog and Other Stories
books.author: Anton Chekhov
books.desc: A collection of Chekhov's stories, led by the tale of a married man and a married woman who meet on holiday in Yalta and cannot forget each other.
about: In the title story, Dmitri Gurov, a Moscow banker unhappily married and used to brief affairs, notices a young woman walking her dog on the seafront at Yalta. She is Anna Sergeyevna, also married and holidaying alone. What begins as another passing adventure turns into a love that neither of them can escape when they return to their ordinary lives. The volume gathers this story with other tales by Chekhov.

Chekhov's stories observe ordinary people with sympathy and without moral judgement, and often leave their endings open. They are known for their economy, their quiet irony and their attention to small details of everyday life.
The Lady with the Dog was first published in December 1899 in the journal Russkaya Mysl. This collection belongs to the series of Chekhov's tales translated into English by Constance Garnett.
books.author_short: Russian short-story writer and playwright (1860–1904), a physician by training, author of Uncle Vanya, Three Sisters and The Cherry Orchard.
author_long: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov was born on 29 January 1860 in Taganrog, in southern Russia. He studied medicine in Moscow, graduating in 1884, while supporting his family by writing comic sketches for magazines, and he continued to practise as a doctor. Suffering from tuberculosis, he spent much of his last years in Yalta, in the Crimea. He died of the disease in July 1904 at the German spa town of Badenweiler, aged 44.
He wrote hundreds of stories, from comic sketches to longer tales such as The Lady with the Dog. His plays include Uncle Vanya (1897), Three Sisters (1901) and The Cherry Orchard (1904).
